title: From registration to insight: how STRONG AYA transforms registry data to enhance decision-support tools for adolescent and young adult oncology
headline: A UK cancer registry joins a European data network
post:
A regional UK cancer registry can contribute to a cross-European data infrastructure for adolescents and young adults with cancer, with the analyses brought into patient consultations.

Work by Joshi Hogenboom, Varsha Gouthamchand, Aiara Lobo Gomes, Andre Dekker and Leonard Wee with colleagues in the STRONG AYA consortium and the University of Leeds.

Data from the Yorkshire Specialist Register of Cancer in Children and Young People were imported into an open-source, privacy-enhancing federated learning infrastructure and analysed together with data from other consortium members. The results go into PROMPT, software from the University of Leeds and Leeds Teaching Hospitals, and into patients' electronic health records.

Health care professionals can view a patient's reported outcomes at different time points next to summary analyses from the wider STRONG AYA infrastructure. The authors see potential for research and policy-making for this group of patients.

The full paper is linked in the comments.

Published in ESMO Real World Data and Digital Oncology.
